full_judgment:
39. In the case of Raghova vs Anandabai reported in AIR 1930 Nag 40 it was held that a customary right can be acquired only in favour of a class or community. The Privy Council in the case of Lakshinder Misra vs Rangalal, AIR 1950 PC 56 observed that— 

 42. There should not be any doubt that after the partition of Pakistan when Sylhet became a part of the then East Pakistan, all the fisheries including Mohal Shamil Jolkors came under the ownership and control of the then East Pakistan Government, at present Bangladesh Government. From the memo dated 17-7-1964 (Annexure-B) it appears that 175 fisheries were enlisted as big fisheries by the then Government of East Pakistan for lease after the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 came into force. The people of former Jainta Porgona could have challenged the inclusion of 175 fisheries in the government lists as their right to catch fish as of customary right was infringed by that inclusion. Since the people of the locality accepted the government decision of would not be wise to open a new debate on that issue.
